svg.text: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W · 3-axis 10K joystick (JH-D300X) · 6 buttons · board seen from the top, USB at the top
Outer legs: + to 3V3, − to AGND. Middle (W) to its ADC pin.
One leg to the GPIO pin, the other leg chained to GND.
VBUS (USB 5 V) charges the battery. Charger OUT feeds VSYS
through a Schottky diode (e.g. 1N5817), so USB and the
battery never fight. Add a power switch on the BAT line.
• Pots get 3V3 (pin 36), never 5 V or VBUS: the analog inputs read 0–3.3 V. Use AGND (pin 33) for the pots, it's the quiet ground.
• All three analog inputs on the Pico 2 W are used (GP26/27/28). More analog controls later need an add-on ADC chip (e.g. ADS1115).
• Buttons need no resistors: the firmware turns on the Pico's internal pull-ups. Pressed = reads low.
• Optional: a 0.1 µF capacitor from each wiper (W) to AGND steadies the readings. Dots mark joined wires; wires that only cross aren't joined.
